column1: # Checks that guard a real bug: check name, tab, issue or pull request, tab,
# what broke. A failing check listed here prints a "guards:" line naming it.
# A name with a / is a test file (tests/ui/...). Every bug fix adds its check
# here; python3 tests/lib/check-regressions.py fails when a name is gone.

directory times from the layer, nested, in two layers, opaque, with a whiteout made in them, 0, after 2038, behind a symlink

a registry taken off the list must be refused again, without a restart

saving from kiri registry must keep the other keys a hand-edited daemon.json has

docker info listed no Registry Mirrors

a container given the engine's socket could change Kiri's registry settings

a path named again as another kind in a later layer

inspect did not show Docker's default MaskedPaths and ReadonlyPaths

a build for another platform from a tag already pulled locally took the local image's platform instead of asking the registry
leaving registry tags to the registry must still serve images built, loaded or tagged only here

--security-opt seccomp:unconfined gave no warning that Kiri keeps its host boundary

a default container without seccomp=unconfined must return empty Warnings
io_uring_setup must stay blocked with EPERM even under seccomp=unconfined

disconnecting the last external network must leave a container on --internal networks with no default route

an --internal IPv6 network on eth0 must never supply an IPv6 default route
disconnecting the external IPv6 network that holds the IPv6 default route must hand the default route over to the next remaining external IPv6 network

docker cp out of and into a created or stopped container ignored directory and file bind mounts (while tmpfs mounts must remain unmounted when not running)
docker cp on a created or stopped container with nested mounts must apply mounts parent-first regardless of argument order
PUT /containers/{id}/archive into a read-only (:ro) volume or bind mount on a running or stopped container must fail with 403 Forbidden and "mounted volume is marked read-only" before writing
PUT /containers/{id}/archive onto a --read-only container rootfs must fail with 403 Forbidden and "container rootfs is marked read-only" while allowing writes into :rw volumes
mount target lookup and docker cp path resolution on a non-running container must confine symlinks inside the container rootfs without escaping onto the host or VM filesystem
the arm64 guest kernel vDSO was linked with DT_GNU_HASH only, so macOS 14's Rosetta aborted every linux/amd64 container with "Failed to find vdso DT_HASH"
removing an image left its unpacked layers in /var/lib/kiri/layers and in docker system df until the next VM boot
docker rmi left the removed image's unpacked layer directory and .done marker on disk in /var/lib/kiri/layers
layer GC after overwriting a tag must keep layers still used by an existing container and reclaim them once that container is removed

a port published on 127.0.0.1 was unreachable from a --network host container at 127.0.0.1 (Mac): connection refused
the same for a port published on every address
a --network host container asked the Mac's resolver for the VM network directly, with no fallback when it refused

a standalone root-run Linux daemon put its 0600 socket under /root/.kiri/run/docker.sock instead of a 0660 /run/kiri/docker.sock, locking out containerized SDK clients whose numeric uid has no host account
the macOS VM data disk stayed fixed at 64 GiB instead of growing via KIRI_DISK_GB / vm.json and online ext4 resize
Settings -> Resources had no Disk image size control for macOS VM disk growth without shrinking
Settings → Storage had no way to move images, containers, volumes and the VM disk to another folder or external drive, or recover when an external drive is unplugged
POST /networks/create with EnableIPv6 false (or omitted) and an IPv6 subnet in IPAM.Config was refused instead of ignoring the IPv6 subnet as Docker does (mailcow-dockerized)
an RFC 9112 §3.2.2 absolute-form request-target over the Docker socket left the scheme and authority in the path and answered 404
docker-modem requests such as GET http://127.0.0.1:2376/containers/json HTTP/1.1 over the Docker socket answered 404 instead of routing /containers/json
importing a container with a Docker Desktop /host_mnt bind-mount source did not translate the path to the host path
imported container HostConfig.Binds kept the /host_mnt prefix or dropped bind mount options instead of stripping /host_mnt
a container imported with a /host_mnt bind source mounted an empty VM directory instead of the host files
kiri import had no way to bring a container's writable layer into Kiri, so files it wrote outside its volumes were lost
a container's imported writable layer must show in docker diff before its first start
a container's imported writable layer must count in docker system df (SizeRw) before its first start
files added and changed in an imported writable layer (owners, modes, links) were missing once the container started
a file the source container deleted from its image came back after import (its whiteout was lost)
an imported writable layer must never be written under a running container's mounted root
Docker Desktop import dropped each container's writable layer (data outside volumes was lost)
reading a container's writable layer must leave no container behind on the source
a directory changed only because a file was added to it must not bring all of its unchanged files
an imported container started without the files it wrote outside its volumes
disconnecting a running container from its only network was refused (or left its veth, routes, and published ports active instead of isolating it)
reconnecting a running container after leaving its first network failed to restore veth connectivity, DNS aliases, or published ports
disconnecting a running container's first network when attached to a second network failed to isolate the left network, promote the default route, or rebind published ports

publishing a container port on a Windows host interface IP (-p IP:port:port) failed inside WSL 2 with EADDRNOTAVAIL (os error 99) instead of binding WSL's eth0 address for kiri-win to forward

build steps under docker build and docker build --network=host (or a host-network builder) could not resolve names through a loopback stub resolver on the host (#330)

on a Linux host, a container with network_mode: host and published ports bound host port forwarders in the shared host netns, causing the container's own listener to fail with EADDRINUSE and populating NetworkSettings.Ports instead of {}

loading an archive whose blobs/sha256/<hex> path already existed in the store could bypass or corrupt content verification if tampered bytes matched the stored size
multi-platform nested OCI index archives needed host-platform resolution and io.containerd.image.name annotation handling
POST /images/load?platform=... did not select the requested platform from a multi-platform OCI index
